lg.l: iruvicum patira muḻaṅki vāṉaviṉ
ṟikuppeya laḻituḷi talaii vāṉam
paruvañ ceyta pāṉāṭ kaṅku
lāṭutalait turuviṉ ṟōṭē mārppak
kaṭaikōṟ ciṟutī yaṭaiya māṭṭit
tiṇkā luṟiyaṉ pāṉaiya ṉakala
nuṇpaḵ ṟuvalai yorutiṟa naṉaippat
taṇṭukā lūṉṟiya taṉinilai yiṭaiyaṉ
maṭiviṭu vīḷai kaṭituceṉ ṟicaippat
teṟimaṟi pārkkuṅ kuṟunari verīi
muḷḷuṭai kuṟuntū ṟiriyap pōkun
taṇṇaṟum puṟavi ṉatuvē naṟumalar
mullai cāṉṟa kaṟpiṉ
melliyaṟ kuṟumaka ḷuṟaivi ṉūrē.
It [is] in the cool fragrant woodland,
where at night, midnight when the season makes
clouds, showering dwindling drops of breaking rain,
clouds uttering thunder so that the dark sky shakes,
the solitary shepherd, who leans on [his] staff,
while the fine many drops wet [him] on one side,
so that he departs, he with a pot, he with a net with firm threads,
after having kindled to settle by a small fire from the end of the sticks,
while the flock of sheep with moving heads bleat in confusion,
goes, so that the short jackal, that is on the lookout for leaping lambs,
is frightened [and] retreats into the thorny small bushes,
when a whistling sounds, moving quickly, emanating from the cloth,
– the village pleasing to stay of the little woman with soft nature,
in [her] fidelity worthy of jasmine with fragrant blossoms.
